probes.note: no such key: cJSON_SetValuestring's OWN `object == NULL` guard, and the one call the mode must skip (cJSON_SetNumberHelper has no NULL check at all -- sn=-)
cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive on an ARRAY answers NULL, so the whole document path takes its no-target branch
same for a scalar root -- the lookup has no child list to walk
an unparseable document is NOT an error in this mode (rc=0, doc=-): the setters are the surface under test and must still run. Every other mode exits 1 here
empty document: ParseWithLength(.., 0) fails, same no-target path
the ordinary path: a NUMBER target, so cJSON_SetValuestring refuses it (not a cJSON_String) and cJSON_SetNumberHelper owns it
setting 0 over an existing number, with an EMPTY replacement string
-0.0: valueint is 0 and the sign survives only in valuedouble's bits, which is why the descriptor carries bits rather than a formatted float
-7.5 truncates TOWARD ZERO into valueint (-7) while valuedouble stays exact
3e9 > INT_MAX: the first saturation guard (cJSON.c:386)
-3e9 < INT_MIN: the second saturation guard
exactly INT_MAX as a double: `number >= INT_MAX` is TRUE, so it saturates rather than casting -- the boundary is inclusive
one representable step below: the cast branch, not the guard
exactly INT_MIN as a double: `number <= (double)INT_MIN` is TRUE, also inclusive
+inf saturates to INT_MAX and PRINTS as null (cJSON refuses to emit a non-finite number)
-inf saturates to INT_MIN, prints null
1e308: finite but far past INT_MAX; prints in full precision
the smallest positive subnormal: valueint 0, valuedouble non-zero
0.5 truncates to 0 -- a number whose valueint and valuedouble disagree, which is what the printer's integer fast-path keys off
duplicate keys: the C walks the child list and stops at the FIRST match, so only the first is set
this mode uses cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive, so `k` does not find `K` -- no target
empty key AND empty replacement: s2 is CreateString(""), then set to "" -- strlen(new) <= strlen(old) with both zero
s2's old text is 1 byte and the new is 16: the ALLOCATING side of cJSON.c:416. Crossed, but not distinguishable from outside -- both paths leave the same valuestring
the reverse: the in-place strcpy side of the same branch
exactly equal lengths -- `<=` makes this the in-place side, so the boundary is pinned
a replacement needing JSON escaping: the descriptor carries the RAW bytes (length-prefixed) and the printed form separately
an interior NUL in the replacement: cJSON_SetValuestring takes a `const char *`, so it copies "ab" and the rest is gone (LESSONS #29). Needs stdin_b64 -- a JSON string cannot spell it (LESSONS #36)
an interior NUL in the KEY: the driver hands cJSON a C string, so the lookup is for `k` and it FINDS the target
bytes 0x80-0xFF in the replacement: cJSON copies string content verbatim with no UTF-8 validation, and the printer emits them raw
a control byte: printed as \u0001, so the raw bytes and the printed form differ
a PARSED string carrying an interior NUL, but NOT targeted: pins that the descriptor's byte fields are C-string fields (the `set` target here is absent)
a non-hex bits field reads as 0 on both sides before any double exists
an empty bits field is also 0 -- the field is optional in effect, never an error
uppercase hex digits are accepted, giving +inf
17 hex digits: only the first 16 are read, so the trailing nibble is ignored rather than shifting the value
the scan stops at the first non-hex character, so this is 0x3ff0 -- a tiny subnormal, not 1.0
a single digit: 0x8, the eighth subnormal
a nested document, target at top level: the rest of the tree must come back unchanged in doc=
no newline: usage error, rc 2 with nothing on stdout
only one tab: usage error
no tabs at all: usage error
the tabs must be in the HEAD line; one after the newline does not count
